quickAnswer.question: How much does a Thailand package cost from Trivandrum?
quickAnswer.answer: iWay Tourism's Thailand packages from Trivandrum start at ₹40,000 per person for a budget 5N/6D Bangkok-Pattaya trip. The standard 6N/7D package including Bangkok and Phuket or Krabi ranges from ₹55,000–₹70,000. All packages include return flights from TRV, visa-on-arrival assistance, hotel accommodation, transfers, sightseeing, and a dedicated iWay coordinator.

overview: Thailand is South India's most versatile international destination — it works for honeymooners, families with children, friend groups, and corporate incentive trips with equal effectiveness. Bangkok delivers temple grandeur and the world's best street food. Phuket offers Andaman Sea beaches backed by five-star resort infrastructure. Krabi provides raw limestone-island beauty accessible by long-tail boat. Pattaya serves as a convenient beach-plus-entertainment hub close to Bangkok.

iWay Tourism designs Thailand packages around a simple principle: pick two or three zones, not all four. The aggregator mistake is cramming Bangkok + Pattaya + Phuket + Krabi into 6 days, resulting in three domestic flights and zero relaxation. Our standard packages pair Bangkok (2 nights) with either Phuket or Krabi (3–4 nights), giving you enough time to actually experience each place rather than just photograph it from a bus window.

visaInfo.heading: Thailand Visa for Indian Passport Holders

quickAnswer.question: Do Indians need a visa for Thailand?
quickAnswer.answer: Indian passport holders can obtain a Visa on Arrival (VoA) at Thai airports for stays up to 15 days. The VoA costs THB 2,000 (approximately ₹5,000) and is processed at the airport immigration counter. Alternatively, a pre-approved e-visa can be obtained online for longer stays. iWay Tourism provides VoA documentation guidance and assists with the process at the airport.

body: Thailand Visa on Arrival requirements: valid passport (minimum 6 months validity, at least 2 blank pages), completed arrival card, return flight ticket within 15 days, proof of accommodation, recent passport photograph, and proof of sufficient funds (THB 10,000 per person or THB 20,000 per family).
The VoA counter at Suvarnabhumi Airport typically processes applications in 15–30 minutes. During peak season, wait times can extend to 1 hour.
iWay Tourism prepares all VoA documentation before departure — arrival card pre-filled, photographs ready, hotel confirmations printed — so the airport process is as fast as possible.

bestTimeToVisit.heading: Best Time to Visit Thailand

quickAnswer.question: When is the best time to visit Thailand from India?
quickAnswer.answer: November to February is Thailand's peak season — cool, dry weather across the country. Bangkok is most comfortable (25–30°C), and the Andaman coast (Phuket, Krabi) has calm, clear seas ideal for island tours and snorkelling. March–May is hot season. June–October is monsoon — cheaper but with afternoon rains and rough seas on the Andaman coast.

bestTimeToVisit.body: Thailand has three seasons: cool and dry (November–February), hot (March–May), and rainy (June–October). For beach-focused trips to Phuket or Krabi, November to April offers the calmest seas and best visibility for snorkelling. Bangkok is a year-round city but most pleasant from November to February. The rainy season brings lower prices and fewer crowds but limits island-hopping on the Andaman coast. For the best balance of weather and value, aim for November or late February.

faqs.question: Phuket or Krabi — which should I choose?
faqs.answer: Phuket suits those who want resort infrastructure, nightlife (Patong), shopping, and the iconic Phi Phi Islands day trip. Krabi suits those who prefer a quieter, more natural setting — Railay Beach is accessible only by boat, the Four Islands tour is less crowded than Phi Phi, and the limestone landscape is more dramatic. Families with young children often prefer Krabi's calmer beaches. Party-oriented groups and first-time Thailand visitors typically prefer Phuket.

faqs.question: Is Thai food too spicy for South Indians?
faqs.answer: South Indians generally handle Thai spice levels well — the chilli heat is comparable to Andhra or Kerala cuisine. The bigger adjustment is the flavour profile: Thai cooking uses lemongrass, galangal, fish sauce, and kaffir lime leaves, which are different from the cumin-coriander-turmeric base of Indian cooking. Vegetarian options exist but require communication — Thai 'vegetarian' dishes may contain fish sauce or shrimp paste. Our restaurant guide flags genuinely vegetarian-friendly establishments.

faqs.question: Can I combine Thailand with another destination?
faqs.answer: Yes. The most natural combinations from Bangkok are: Thailand + Singapore (2.5-hour flight), Thailand + Vietnam (2-hour flight to Hanoi), or Thailand + Bali (4-hour flight). iWay Tourism designs multi-destination itineraries that optimise flight routing and visa logistics across countries.
